title: ClearPath Managed IT Services Exit Billing Basis
content:
**Clause.** The monthly basis of the early termination fee of a ClearPath Managed IT Services agreement, that is the monthly amount to which the exit-fee percentage and the months charged are applied, follows the exit billing-basis rule. The rule reads the monthly fees posted in the last 3 months (a month window ending today) and the covered seats on the seat ledger (every seat addition less every seat removal), compared with the minimum-commitment floor (the contracted seats multiplied by the tier's minimum seat commitment percentage and divided by 100, rounded up to a whole seat):

(a) when three or more monthly fees were posted in that window and the covered seats exceed the floor, the basis is the average of the monthly fees posted in that window, their sum divided by their number;

(b) when fewer than three were posted and the covered seats exceed the floor, the basis is the per-seat rate multiplied by the covered seats;

(c) otherwise the basis is the per-seat rate multiplied by the floor seats.

A whole month between two dates is counted only once the later date reaches the same day of the month as the earlier one, and a month window of N months ending today takes the entries dated fewer than N whole months before today. The monthly fees counted are the monthly fee entries on the agreement's billing ledger, by posting date.

**Combinations.**

| Monthly fees posted in the last 3 months | Covered seats on the ledger | Monthly basis |
|---|---|---|
| 3 or more | above the floor | average of those monthly fees |
| fewer than 3 | above the floor | per-seat rate times covered seats |
| any | at or below the floor | per-seat rate times floor seats |

**Hypothetical case.** Floor 21 seats, 25 covered seats, per-seat rate 100.00. Monthly fees of 2500.00, 2500.00 and 2600.00 posted in the window: the basis is 7600.00 divided by 3, that is 2533.333.... With only two fees in the window the basis is 2500.00 (25 seats); with 21 covered seats it is 2100.00.
